codeReview.summary: The tab scaffold mostly matches the requested layout and URL deep-linking, but it does not actually preserve existing functionality: the committed diff regressed the Delivery Log tab to the old filter/results card UI instead of keeping the current table/filter/pagination implementation already present on main, so the feature fails the no-regressions requirement.

issues.description: The feature imports and renders the legacy `OpsEmailDeliveryFiltersCard`/`OpsEmailDeliveryResultsCard` flow in the Delivery Log tab rather than preserving the current table-based delivery log implementation. In the reviewed repository state, `tab-layout-scaffold` is supposed to scaffold tabs without regressing existing functionality, but commit `8ea99697` replaces the newer `OpsEmailDeliveryFilterBar` + `OpsEmailDeliveryTable` + rich pagination/error handling path with the older card UI, violating the feature requirement that existing functionality be preserved and failing VAL-CROSS-005's cross-tab header/content expectations for the current page.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission shared state says the dev harness is available at `http://localhost:3000/dev/ops-email-delivery`, but mission AGENTS and the worker handoff both note a pre-existing `APP_ENV=staging` setup that causes `enforceDevOnly()` to return 404 locally. The current shared-state docs do not reconcile that contradiction.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/user-testing.md declares the dev harness as no-auth primary surface, while mission AGENTS.md `Known Pre-Existing Issues` says `/dev/ops-email-delivery` returns 404 because `APP_ENV=staging` is set in `.env.local`; handoff.discoveredIssues repeats the same blocker.

summary: Review failed: tab switching and URL parsing were added, but the committed scaffold regresses the Delivery Log tab back to legacy cards instead of preserving the current table/filter/pagination implementation, so the feature does not safely satisfy its no-regression requirement. Shared-state docs also conflict on whether the dev harness is usable in the present environment.
